row.name: Childrens Lighthouse Learning Center at Stone Oak

occurrences.finding: Children Handwashing After Toileting or Diapering: A child in room 3 hand's were not washed after being on the diaper change table.     **Corrected at inspection when the caregiver was asked and washed the child's hands at the sink.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Children Handwashing After Toileting or Diapering (26 TAC §746.3417(3))

occurrences.finding: Cots, Beds, Mats Labeled With Child's Name: In the preschool classrooms, the children were not sleeping on their assigned cots.       *Corrected during the inspection when the nap map was updated with the correct name and number for each child.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Cots, Beds, Mats Labeled With Child's Name (26 TAC §746.4503(b))

occurrences.finding: Responsibilities of Employees and Caregivers -Demonstrate Competency, Good Judgment, Self-control: During the course of the investigation, it was determined that a caregiver did not demonstrate good judgement when she placed two infant bottles right next to each other just prior to feeding, then did not take the time to accurately identify the bottles before feeding them to the infants, leading to her feeding the incorrect bottle to an infant.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Responsibilities of Employees and Caregivers -Demonstrate Competency, Good Judgment, Self-control (26 TAC §746.1201(1))

occurrences.finding: Responsibilities of Caregivers - Know number of children responsible for: Caregiver provided the incorrect number of children in their care. Caregiver reported she had eight children in the classroom when there were seven children in the classroom.    Note: This was corrected at inspection when the director had the caregiver verify the number of children in care. Caregiver confirmed there were six children in the classroom.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Responsibilities of Caregivers - Know number of children responsible for (26 TAC §746.1205(a)(2))

occurrences.finding: Child/ Caregiver Ratio - 13 or More Children: Twenty four school age children ages five to six years old were in the classroom with one caregiver. The specified age group was five years old, resulting in the classroom being over ratio by two children.    Note: This was corrected at inspection when the director stayed in the classroom until a second caregiver was placed in the classroom.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Child/ Caregiver Ratio - 13 or More Children (26 TAC §746.1601)

occurrences.finding: Responsibilities of Caregivers - Know number of children responsible for: The caregiver in the after school classroom gave the incorrect number of children in care in the classroom. Caregiver stated there were twenty-six children in care when there were twenty-five children in the classroom.      Note: This was corrected at inspection when caregiver recounted the children and provided the correct number of children in their care.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Responsibilities of Caregivers - Know number of children responsible for (26 TAC §746.1205(a)(2))

occurrences.finding: Supervision ensures each child?s safety, well-being, including physical proximity and auditory or visual awareness of each child?s on going activity: During an investigation, it was determined a child exited their classroom when parent opened the door to the classroom. Child was unsupervised for approximately forty-five seconds until found.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Supervision ensures each child?s safety, well-being, including physical proximity and auditory or visual awareness of each child?s on going activity (26 TAC §746.1205(a)(4))

occurrences.finding: Supervision ensures each child?s safety, well-being, including physical proximity and auditory or visual awareness of each child?s on going activity: Based on information gathered, caregiver was not actively supervising the children appropriately. Caregiver did not intervene when one child was on top of small bookshelf, and another child pushed the child who was on top of the bookshelf, causing child to fall over the bookshelf and the bookshelf flipping over and falling on child, causing a bruise near the eye.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Supervision ensures each child?s safety, well-being, including physical proximity and auditory or visual awareness of each child?s on going activity (26 TAC §746.1205(a)(4))

occurrences.finding: Responsibilities of Employees and Caregivers -Demonstrate Competency, Good Judgment, Self-control: The caregiver did not demonstrate good judgment when seen on video footage lifting a child by the left hand/wrist off the floor before getting a hold of the child?s right hand/wrist, extending both arms, and placing the child in the chair, which resulted in an accidental injury that required medical attention.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Responsibilities of Employees and Caregivers -Demonstrate Competency, Good Judgment, Self-control (26 TAC §746.1201(1))

occurrences.finding: AP Background check results - Must receive notification prior to allowing subject to be present at your operation: A staff member who had direct access to children in care did not have a background check from the CBCU regarding the persons eligibility.     Note: This was corrected at inspection when caregiver was sent home.
occurrences.violation_type_title: AP Background check results - Must receive notification prior to allowing subject to be present at your operation (26 TAC §745.641)

occurrences.finding: Supervision ensures each child?s safety, well-being, including physical proximity and auditory or visual awareness of each child?s on going activity: During the investigation, it was determined a child exited the classroom and was unsupervised for approximately 4 minutes.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Supervision ensures each child?s safety, well-being, including physical proximity and auditory or visual awareness of each child?s on going activity (26 TAC §746.1205(a)(4))

occurrences.finding: Parental Communication - Situation that Placed a Child at Risk: During the investigation, it was determined the operation did not immediately notify the parents, when their child walked out of the classroom and was found unsupervised.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Parental Communication - Situation that Placed a Child at Risk (26 TAC §746.307(b)(4))

occurrences.finding: Supervision ensures each child?s safety, well-being, including physical proximity and auditory or visual awareness of each child?s on going activity: During the investigation, it was determined a child exited the classroom and was unsupervised for approximately 8 minutes.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Supervision ensures each child?s safety, well-being, including physical proximity and auditory or visual awareness of each child?s on going activity (26 TAC §746.1205(a)(4))

occurrences.finding: Supervision ensures each child?s safety, well-being, including physical proximity and auditory or visual awareness of each child?s on going activity: Supervision was compromised when a child was left unattended in the hallway for approximately four minutes and thirty seconds. It was not discovered, and that child was unattended until a parent opened the door and the child was let into the classroom..
occurrences.violation_type_title: Supervision ensures each child?s safety, well-being, including physical proximity and auditory or visual awareness of each child?s on going activity (26 TAC §746.1205(a)(4))

occurrences.finding: Installation and Maintenance of Loose-fill Surfacing - Six Inches if Equipment 5 Ft or Less: At the base of each slide on all three playgrounds the loose fill was not at required 6-inch depth.   *This was created at inspection when staff filled the loose fill on the base of each slide on all three playgrounds to the required 6-inch depth.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Installation and Maintenance of Loose-fill Surfacing - Six Inches if Equipment 5 Ft or Less (26 TAC §746.4907(a)(1))

occurrences.finding: Prohibited Punishments - Grabbing and Pulling: Based on video footage obtained, a caregiver was observed forcibly approaching a young child and positioning herself over the child lying on a mat while grabbing the child's face in an attempt to address her behavior during rest time.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Prohibited Punishments - Grabbing and Pulling (26 TAC §746.2805(3))

occurrences.finding: Supervision ensures each child?s safety, well-being, including physical proximity and auditory or visual awareness of each child?s on going activity: Supervision was compromised when caregivers left a small child unsupervised on the playground.  The caregivers who were on a separate playground found the child approximately 15- 30 minutes later and alerted management.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Supervision ensures each child?s safety, well-being, including physical proximity and auditory or visual awareness of each child?s on going activity (26 TAC §746.1205(a)(4))

occurrences.finding: Parental Communication - Situation that Placed a Child at Risk: The parent whose child was left unsupervised on the playground was not notified immediately after the incident occurred. The incident occurred on October 11, 2024, and the parent was not notified about the incident until October 23, 2024.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Parental Communication - Situation that Placed a Child at Risk (26 TAC §746.307(b)(4))

occurrences.finding: Director Responsibilities - Operate in Compliance: The center director failed to meet her responsibilities and did not inform the parent of a child who had been placed at risk even after she had been notified that an investigation was opened regarding the incident.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Director Responsibilities - Operate in Compliance (26 TAC §746.1003(1))

occurrences.finding: Licensing Incident/Illness Report Form - Situations Placing Children at Risk: An incident report for an incident that placed a child at risk was not provided to the parent within 48 hours.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Licensing Incident/Illness Report Form - Situations Placing Children at Risk (26 TAC §746.701(5))

occurrences.finding: Report Situation Placing Children at Risk: It was determined in a DFPS investigation that an incident that occurred on 10/11/2024 where a child was left unsupervised on a playground was not reported in the required 48 hour timeframe.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Report Situation Placing Children at Risk (26 TAC §746.305(a)(6))

occurrences.finding: Annual Fire Inspection - Before Initial Permit Issued and Every 12 Months: Documentation of a fire inspection being completed within the last 12 months was not available for review.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Annual Fire Inspection - Before Initial Permit Issued and Every 12 Months (26 TAC §746.5101(a))

occurrences.finding: Safety - Play Materials and Equipment Safe: A shelf in the infant classroom was observed to have peeling safety coating.    A large hole about 5-12 inches wide and 5-12 inches deep was observed in the school age playground.    Exposed piping was observed in the school age playground.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Safety - Play Materials and Equipment Safe (26 TAC §746.3701(5))

occurrences.finding: Written Feeding Instructions - Review and Update Every 30 Days: Infant monthly feeding sheets for the month of June have not been signed.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Written Feeding Instructions - Review and Update Every 30 Days (26 TAC §746.2421(b))

occurrences.finding: Documentation of Drills: Documentation for drills was not readily available to include Severe weather, fire, smoke, and extinguisher checks were missing for May.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Documentation of Drills (26 TAC §746.5205(4))

occurrences.finding: Required Equipment in Vehicles - First-aid Kit: First aid kit in van #1 was missing thermometer and tweezers   Van #2 was missing themomerter, scissors, tweezers  Van # 3 did not have a first aid kit at all
occurrences.violation_type_title: Required Equipment in Vehicles - First-aid Kit (26 TAC §746.5617(a)(6))

occurrences.finding: AP Background check results - Must receive notification prior to allowing subject to be present at your operation: There was one staff member employed with the operation that did not have cleared background check.    Note: The employee was immediately sent home for the day.
occurrences.violation_type_title: AP Background check results - Must receive notification prior to allowing subject to be present at your operation (26 TAC §745.641)
